messages:
marco: Heads-up question: should the gateway surface an explicit "stream-stable" signal to the edge once the first server chunk is acked by the client? We're trying to avoid mid-stream hedges replaying side effects.
anya: Sort of like 'we've reached on-client-visible state; stop speculative retries' ? makes sense.
dinesh: Yes. We've seen hedges that trigger DB double-writes when the client already received a partial success.
cory: Two concerns: (1) interop/rollout with older edges, (2) how this interacts with resume/checkpoint semantics.
marco: Proposal: gateway adds header `x-rw-stream-stable: 1` when it has observed client ACK of the first chunk (or after sending first chunk for HTTP/1 clients). The edge runtime then demotes retry policy for that request id to "no speculative hedging".
anya: For resumable streams, the runtime can emit an opaque trailer: `x-rw-resume-id: v2:<enc>` and optionally `x-rw-resume-ok: true`. Gateway persists resume-id and offers resume API to clients.
dinesh: Important: edge must still be able to retry idempotent reads. So change is to reduce hedging, not to disable all retries. Maybe map: hedging_window=0, simple linear backoff retries for idempotent only.
cory: Observability: add traces and metrics: `edge.stream_stable.received`, `edge.stream_stable.hedge_suppressed`, `gateway.resume.persisted`. Also surface a span tag `stream.stable=true`.
marco: Billing/product: if stream-stable is set and client disconnects, do we bill full request? Product wants a deterministic rule. Suggestion: bill up to last persisted resume checkpoint. If resume-id present -> billable until checkpoint. If not -> bill up to last chunk sent.
anya: Security: resume tokens must be short-lived, encrypted, and customer-scoped. Gateway should only hand out a resume token id (not raw data) unless customer opts in. Store payload in KVS with TTL and audit log.
dinesh: Rollout plan: gateway emits `x-rw-stream-stable` only to edges advertising runtime >= 1.9 with feature flag `stream-stable`. Older edges ignore header. We should also add a compatibility header `x-rw-features: stream-stable` in discovery.
cory: Edge behavior details proposal:
- On `x-rw-stream-stable` -> set hedging_window=0 for request id, record trace tag
- If runtime can produce resume token, write trailer `x-rw-resume-id` at stream end and persist to cluster KVS
- If no trailer emitted -> mark request "partial_no_resume" and require client-provided idempotency-key for server-side replay paths
marco: One more wrinkle: what about multi-hop proxies? Gateway->frontdoor->edge. Need to propagate the signal across hops and ensure only the first hop that observed client ack flips the flag. Maybe header should include `x-rw-stream-stable-origin: <gateway-id>` and hops should preserve it.
anya: Good call. Also add a TTL on resume tokens and a single-use flag to prevent replay abuse.
dinesh: Ops: we need admin APIs to list and revoke resume tokens for debugging. Metrics: `edge.resume.tokens_created`, `edge.resume.tokens_revoked`.
cory: Implementation risk: if gateway incorrectly marks stream-stable too early (e.g., lost ACKs), we could prematurely suppress necessary retries. So add telemetry to track suppressed retries that would have succeeded.
marco: Agreed. We'll stage in canary: gateway v2.6 feature-flagged, edge runtime 1.9+, monitor `edge.quiesce.miss_rate`.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: gateway v2.6 canary -> staging (owner: @marco). :rocket:
anya: I'll draft an RFC covering header/trailer names, KVS storage schema (opaque id only), metrics, rollout checklist, and sample trace instrumentation. Can everyone +1 in thread before EOD?
cory: +1
dinesh: +1
marco: Thanks all, i'll post RFC link shortly. :thumbsup:
